title: Great Minds Think Alike: Contextual Tacit Communication for Decentralized LLM-Agent Cooperation
claim: Coordination signals from a centralized joint scorer are distilled offline into retrievable rules that let decentralized agents act consistently without communication.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right flow, arrow from A's distillation down into B's memory
description: Two horizontal bands. Top band (A), Centralized Bias Fitting: a task instruction with a clipboard icon sits at top left. Agent 1…n boxes with robot icons feed a Joint plan u and an Individual LLM Values block. These go to a Joint LLM Value Q_LLM box, with example scores for two joint plans, and then to a Bias fitting module. That module shows q_LLM,i plus b_i giving Q', plus v, and a bar chart of residual δ. An arrow leads to a Context Rule Distillation box. A long arrow runs down to a red TRM database cylinder holding entries e=(r,c,b). Bottom band (B), Decentralized Execution with TRM: a human avatar with a task instruction. Agent 1…n boxes receive role-specific rule prompts (ingredient-chain agent, tool-chain agent) from TRM. Their actions combine into a Joint Plan sent to the Environment. The palette is tan, beige and red on a pale olive background, with purple and yellow highlighted words.
caption: The overview of the framework. (A) A centralized joint LLM scorer evaluates candidate joint plans, while agents produce local values; we fit biases to align corrected local values with the joint judgment and distill them into TRM rules. (B) At execution time, each agent conditions on its local progress plus retrieved rule context from TRM to act without conflicts.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as planners for cooperative embodied agents, but multi-agent settings amplify inconsistency under partial observability and make explicit communication costly or even unavailable. Many existing approaches rely on online message passing; when communication is removed, agents often fall back to independent local planning that suffers from miscoordination. We introduce Contextual Tacit Communication, a gradient-free protocol that aligns decentralized decisions with a joint LLM value score without explicit message actions. Our method measures context-conditioned value rectifications via residual banding to pinpoint miscoordination actions and amortizes the resulting coordination signals into a retrieval-augmented Tacit Rule Memory that provides prompt-level cooperation rules at execution time. Experiments on VIKI, C-WAH, and TDW-MAT show that our approach improves cooperation performance over baselines while reducing runtime overhead compared with communication-based methods.
